summary: This edited volume brings together contributions from across disciplines and domains of expertise to offer thoughtful guidance on AI ethics, law, and policy. The “Ethics” section grapples with broad issues facing institutions amid the ongoing march of AI, such as agency, morality, and personhood, and provides frameworks for ethical decision-making. The “Law” section explores current legal considerations and challenges that are emerging as AI forces us to confront issues of ownership, accountability, and culpability. The “Policy” section provides insight into how institutions, corporations, and governments are navigating these challenges to provide workable solutions. Moreover, a final “Domain Applications” section offers case-study-like examples of how these issues are being addressed in real-world situations, with deep, illustrative detail. Across these chapters, diverse voices offer a wealth of philosophical considerations and practical guidance on how we can lead the world more intentionally toward the AI future we want.
